name: Whist
description: Whist is the classic English partnership trick-taking game and ancestor of Bridge. 4 players, 2 teams. 52 cards, 13 each. Last card dealt (to dealer) turned face-up = trump. Eldest hand leads. Follow suit. Each trick over 6 = 1 point. Honours (A-K-Q-J of trump): 3 held = 2pts, 4 held = 4pts. Game to 5 (British) or 7 (American). Rubber = best of 3.

history.origins: Whist originated in 17th–18th century England, evolving from Ruff and Honours (described in The Complete Gamester, 1674). Played with a full 52-card pack, it superseded its predecessor in the 18th century. The name derives from the period word meaning quiet or attentive. It was first played on scientific principles at London's Crown Coffee House (c. 1728); Edmond Hoyle's 1742 treatise became the standard for a century.
history.evolution: Dominated European card gaming for 200+ years. Ancestor of Bridge.

setup.dealing: 13 each. Last card (to dealer) turned up = trump.

rules.objective: Partnerships aim to win more tricks than the opponents; each odd trick (over six) scores one point. The first side to reach the agreed game target (5 points in Britain, 7 in America) wins the game.
rules.gameplay: Eldest hand leads. Follow suit. Trump if void (optional). Highest trump or highest of led suit wins. Each trick over 6 = 1pt. Honours: 3 of A-K-Q-J trump = 2pts, 4 = 4pts.
